title: A gate that waits in a loop

blocks.text: A thread in `Object.wait()` is `WAITING`: it has released the monitor and waits for a signal. But it "can wake up spuriously without being notified", which is why the page says `wait()` belongs **in a loop that re-checks the condition**. The same loop makes a signal that came before the wait harmless.
Write `Gate`, which uses **the `Gate` object itself** as its monitor:

items: `void pass()` returns at once if the gate is open. While it is closed, the thread waits on the gate's monitor, and it returns only once the gate is open. It declares `throws InterruptedException`.
`void open()` opens the gate for good and wakes every waiting thread.

rows: a thread is woken while the gate is still closed

cases.says: A thread in pass() waits while the gate is closed and goes on once another thread opens it.
While the gate is closed, the waiting thread is WAITING: it neither spins nor sleeps.
A wakeup while the gate is still closed, like a spurious one, sends the waiter back to waiting.
pass() on a gate that is already open returns at once.
open() wakes every waiting thread, so two threads waiting at the closed gate both go through.
The waiting thread waits on the Gate object's own monitor, not on a private lock.

concepts: Object.wait() can wake spuriously, so it is called in a loop that re-checks the condition.
A thread in wait() is WAITING and has released the monitor, unlike a BLOCKED thread that never had it.
